priority-tax-relief.title: Priority Tax Relief
priority-tax-relief.heroSentence: First design hire. 14× more conversion opportunities, and a design kit engineering runs without me.

dossier.role: Brand & Product Designer, first design hire
dossier.team: Solo, embedded with engineering, marketing, and leadership
dossier.stakes: $7M MRR national firm, 200 people, no prior design function
dossier.status: Live: brand system, component library, replatformed site

priority-tax-relief.body: There was no design system, and decisions ran on opinion. I analyzed the full paying-customer database and interviewed stakeholders across departments, then built the brand system and component library engineering now uses without a designer in the room. I also led the WordPress to Django/Wagtail replatform: Lighthouse performance 68 → 91–100, accessibility from 64 issues to AA WCAG.

heroArtifact.alt: Priority Tax Relief brand guideline pages — logo lockups, color system, usage rules

processArtifact.alt: Departmental process-mapping board from cross-department stakeholder research

seattle-creative-directory.title: Seattle Creative Directory
seattle-creative-directory.heroSentence: Nobody asked me to build this. Six years later, it's still running.
seattle-creative-directory.body: No platform connected Seattle's creative and technology community, so I designed and built one: Next.js, PostgreSQL, Prisma, Vercel, with an information architecture covering hundreds of businesses by location, discipline, and organization type. Ongoing community interviews and a podcast (50K+ plays) feed the product direction.

heroArtifact.alt: Seattle Creative Directory homepage — podcast guest quote grid

processArtifact.alt: Seattle Creative Directory filter taxonomy — size, neighborhood, and discipline facets

android-gemini.title: Android Gemini Studies
android-gemini.heroSentence: Gesture first, not a chat box: seven interaction-pattern families for Gemini on Android.

dossier.team: Dedicated interaction designer within a BUCK concept team (creative director, two motion designers, rotating designers)
dossier.stakes: Early Gemini: capability with no native UX paradigm on Android
dossier.status: Internal concept exploration for Google's Gemini team

android-gemini.body: In late 2023 Gemini had capability but no interface model on a phone, and a chat box is wrong for a device that is physical and contextual. I pressure-tested early thinking into seven pattern families across four scenarios: drive-to-output, camera as AI interface, contextual web actions, and AI personality tuning. The through-line was Dots & Handles: AI shouldn't just generate output, it should give you something to grab onto afterward.

heroArtifact.alt: Whats That style-spectrum slider concept frame

processArtifact.alt: Interaction-pattern storyboard exploring three variants of an AI action menu

resonance-ai.title: Resonance AI
resonance-ai.heroSentence: Cut analyst reporting time 95% on an AI product whose output users couldn't verify.

dossier.team: Solo designer, working with engineering and data science
dossier.stakes: Users acting on insights they couldn't independently verify
dossier.status: Shipped to all active clients; drove an acquihire

resonance-ai.body: Users had to act on machine-generated insight with no way to check it. As sole designer I built the visual language from scratch (type, iconography, chart language, color) and the workflows to interpret, validate, and act on that output. Reporting moved from weekly to daily, and the product's value drove an acquihire.

processArtifact.alt: Early chart-language and color-system exploration for the AI output

pwc.title: PwC Concourse
pwc.heroSentence: My touch components became the mobile baseline across PwC's internal products.

dossier.team: Sole designer on the responsive build, within a 12-person design team
dossier.stakes: Enterprise collaboration platform, US and British offices
dossier.status: Shipped: adopted as the mobile baseline platform-wide

pwc.body: The enterprise collaboration platform was desktop-only. I researched how distributed teams in US and British offices manage projects and communication, then turned that into interaction models, reusable patterns, and a responsive adaptation from mobile through 1900px desktop. The components were adopted well beyond this one product.

heroArtifact.alt: PwC Concourse responsive dashboard, anonymized per existing NDA guidance

lumedic.title: Lumedic
lumedic.heroSentence: Spring 2020: tens of thousands of hospital employees had to prove COVID status to get to work. I designed the wallet they used.

dossier.role: Product Designer — primary designer on the patient wallet
dossier.company: Lumedic, a Providence St. Joseph Health portfolio company
dossier.team: Primary designer on this platform within a 5-person design team
dossier.stakes: Trust handshake between patients, hospital verifiers, and issuers
dossier.status: Shipped on iOS, Android, and web across the Providence network

lumedic.body: Patients weren't parties to their own medical records. Lumedic inverted that: the patient holds verified credentials and shares them selectively. I designed three releases across web, iOS, and Android, plus the issuer dashboard clinics used for bulk uploads. Research showed people needed the outcome, not the credential system, so we dropped "blockchain" and most explanatory copy, and trust went up.

heroArtifact.alt: Lumedic verification kiosk — verified COVID-19 status state

processArtifact.alt: Lumedic holder-side flow — add connection, vaccination card, test result detail

providence.title: Providence Telestroke & Express Care
providence.heroSentence: Real-time stroke-response workflows, where a slow or wrong interface affects patient outcomes.

dossier.stakes: Real-time clinical workflow — patient outcomes during stroke response
dossier.status: Shipped: design system adopted by subsequent teams

providence.body: Field research with clinicians showed the assumptions behind the existing design were wrong, and inverted the information hierarchy. I integrated the Epic API for live patient records, adapted Material Design for healthcare, and worked in Storybook with engineering to close handoff gaps. The design system outlasted my time on the project and was adopted by subsequent teams.

heroArtifact.alt: Express Care Virtual information-architecture and workflow diagram

processArtifact.alt: Hand-annotated field research notes on the inverted telestroke hierarchy
